An operator-host shell\n * can retain a dead PAPERCUSP_HONO_PORT after its per-session host exits; the\n * canonical green operator is still a safe recovery target in that case.\n * Keep this fallback limited to the implicit self-port route so an explicit\n * --url or a bare PAPERCUSP_OPERATOR_URL without a self-port remains an\n * authoritative pin.\n *\n * @param {EnvironmentMap} [env]\n * @param {string | null} [explicitUrl]\n * @returns {string[]}\n */\nexport function resolvePtoolOperatorCandidates(env = process.env, explicitUrl = null) {\n  const explicit = typeof explicitUrl === 'string' ? explicitUrl.trim() : '';\n  if (explicit) return [explicit];\n\n  const primary = resolvePtoolOperatorBase(env);\n  const selfPort = typeof env.PAPERCUSP_HONO_PORT === 'string'\n    ? env.PAPERCUSP_HONO_PORT.trim()\n    : '';\n  if (!/^\\d+$/.test(selfPort) || Number(selfPort) < 1 || Number(selfPort) > 65535) return [primary];\n  try {\n    const parsed = new URL(primary);\n    const localHost = parsed.hostname === '127.0.0.1' || parsed.hostname === 'localhost' || parsed.hostname === '::1';\n    const parsedPort = parsed.port || (parsed.protocol === 'https:' ? '443' : '80');\n    if (localHost && selfPort !== '3070' && parsedPort === selfPort) {\n      return [primary, `${parsed.protocol}//127.0.0.1:3070`];\n    }\n  } catch {\n    // connectWithLocalRetry will report malformed primary URLs; do not mask\n    // that diagnostic while resolving an optional fallback.\n  }\n  return [primary];\n}\n\n/**\n * A named call must use the operator selected at invocation start. Otherwise a\n * dead staging listener can silently move a schema-dependent write or replay to\n * an older live operator. Catalog browsing may still recover to another host;\n * callers can then explicitly pin that host with --url for a subsequent call.\n */\n\nfunction describePtoolOperatorRoute(operatorUrl, env = process.env) {\n  try {\n    const url = new URL(operatorUrl);\n    const hostname = url.hostname.toLowerCase();\n    const local = hostname === '127.0.0.1' || hostname === 'localhost' || hostname === '::1';\n    const port = Number(url.port || (url.protocol === 'https:' ? 443 : url.protocol === 'http:' ? 80 : 0));\n    const attemptTimeoutMs = ptoolConnectAttemptTimeoutMs(operatorUrl, env);\n    if (!local) return { routeClass: 'remote', host: hostname, port, attemptTimeoutMs };\n\n    const configuredProxyBase = typeof env.PAPERCUSP_MCP_PROXY_BASE === 'string'\n      ? env.PAPERCUSP_MCP_PROXY_BASE.trim()\n      : '';\n    let matchesProxyBase = false;\n    if (configuredProxyBase) {\n      try {\n        matchesProxyBase = new URL(configuredProxyBase).origin === url.origin;\n      } catch {\n        return { routeClass: 'local-unknown', host: hostname, port, attemptTimeoutMs };\n      }\n    }\n    const configuredProxyPort = Number(env.PAPERCUSP_MCP_PROXY_PORT);\n    const proxyPort = Number.isInteger(configuredProxyPort) && configuredProxyPort > 0\n      ? configuredProxyPort\n      : 9071;\n    return {\n      routeClass: matchesProxyBase || port === proxyPort ? 'local-proxy' : 'local-direct',\n      host: hostname,\n      port,\n      attemptTimeoutMs,\n    };\n  } catch {\n    return { routeClass: 'invalid', host: null, port: null, attemptTimeoutMs: null };\n  }\n}\n\n    url.pathname = `${pathWithoutTrailingSlash}/api/mcp`;\n  }\n  url.searchParams.set('superuser', '1');\n  if (workspace) url.searchParams.set('workspace', workspace);\n  if (harness) url.searchParams.set('harness', harness);\n  if (client) url.searchParams.set('client', client);\n  // A retained owner can have several native incarnations. Prefer the native\n  // session explicitly bound by the launcher; CODEX_SESSION_ID can be stale\n  // in a retained shell and the server correctly rejects that foreign id.\n  // Fall back to Codex's current id for older launch environments. An explicit\n  // endpoint binding wins, and another client's identity must never inherit\n  // this process's native session.\n  const nativeSession = String(nativeSessionOverride !== undefined\n    ? nativeSessionOverride ?? ''\n    : env.PAPERCUSP_NATIVE_SESSION_ID ||\n      (String(env.PAPERCUSP_AGENT ?? '').trim() === 'claude'\n        ? env.CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID\n        : env.CODEX_SESSION_ID) || '').trim();\n  if (!url.searchParams.has('native_session') && nativeSession &&\n      client && client === String(env.PAPERCUSP_SID ?? '').trim()) {\n    url.searchParams.set('native_session', nativeSession);\n  }\n  if (contextTier) url.searchParams.set('ctx_tier', contextTier);\n  return url;\n}\n\n/** A foreign native-session refusal is emitted before the tool dispatcher runs. */\nexport function isForeignNativeSessionRejection(result) {\n  return (result?.isError === true &&\n    Array.isArray(result.content) &&\n    result.content.some((block) =>\n      block?.type === 'text' && block.text === 'request_rejected: superuser_foreign_native_session')) ||\n    /\\bmcp_auth_failed:\\s*superuser_foreign_native_session\\b/.test(errorDetail(result));\n}\n\n/** Retry only an inherited Codex claim; an explicit launcher binding stays authoritative. */\nexport function shouldRetryWithoutNativeSession(result, {\n  client, explicitNativeSession = false, env = process.env,\n} = {}) {\n  return isForeignNativeSessionRejection(result) &&\n    Boolean(String(env.CODEX_SESSION_ID ?? The distinction is measured in thread-post:1161737.\\n\\nCodex 0.160.1 reads MCP environment headers from its process environment while shell-command setup injects the current session identity into the execution environment. Existing mechanism\\n\\nThe superuser MCP transport accepts x-papercusp-native-session or native\\\\_session, verifies that the native ID belongs to the supplied owner, and threads the verified advSessionId into current kernel launch-record selection. The native Codex MCP configuration preserves a legacy process-environment header. For tool calls, the source repair prefers Codex's per-call `_meta.threadId`, then verifies that claim through the same owner/native-session classifier; header and query carriers remain for older clients and non-tool requests. The maintained ptool and scripts/mcp-call.mjs fallbacks now preserve CODEX\\\\_SESSION\\\\_ID automatically when their client is this process's PAPERCUSP\\\\_SID. ptool preserves an explicit native\\\\_session URL; neither helper attaches this native session to another client identity. No authority or role gate is weakened.\\n\\nThe psu launcher strips inherited `CODEX_SESSION_ID` and `PAPERCUSP_NATIVE_SESSION_ID` before starting an independent child. A parent shell's Codex ID can otherwise be paired with the child's Papercusp SID, which the operator rejects as `superuser_foreign_native_session`. The child can supply its own Codex ID after startup; when bootstrap already knows a bound native ID, the explicit launch envelope restores `PAPERCUSP_NATIVE_SESSION_ID` after sanitization.\",\"bytes\":1332,\"sliced\":true}],\"surface\":\"engineering\"}\n","exit_code":0,"duration":{"secs":4,"nanos":848857282}},"started_at_ms":1791596361664,"completed_at_ms":1791596366514}}

Kernel-backed and\n--                         therefore immune to PID reuse, which happens ~daily here under fleet\n--                         load; a bare pid would silently merge two processes into one.\n--   serving_build_sha   — WHAT CODE it loaded. The load-bearing one: a stale host is defined by\n--                         its code, not by its address.\n--\n-- Boot time deliberately gets no column: `min(invoked_at) GROUP BY serving_process_id` bounds it\n-- from the ledger itself.\n--\n-- NULL is a real, meaningful value in all three and must never be backfilled with a guess. For\n-- rows predating this migration it reads as \"recorded before serving-host was tracked\". For\n-- `serving_build_sha` it additionally means the process could not PROVE what bytes it loaded (a\n-- bundled artifact with no baked sha — see lib/build-info.ts, which refuses to report the current\n-- checkout's HEAD in that case). Substituting a plausible sha there would recreate precisely the\n-- false-confidence failure these columns exist to end.\n--\n-- Additive only: three nullable columns, no default, no backfill. ADD COLUMN without a default is\n-- O(1) in PG11+ and this table takes ~800K inserts/day, so it must stay that way.\n--\n-- One partial index, mirroring the shape of tool_invocations_coord_owner_idx: the whole point is\n-- that `SELECT serving_host, status, count(*) … GROUP BY 1,2` is CHEAP, since an expensive\n-- forensic query is one nobody runs during an incident.\n\nALTER TABLE harness_shared.tool_invocations\n  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS serving_host text,\n  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS serving_process_id text,\n  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS serving_build_sha text;\n\nCOMMENT ON COLUMN harness_shared.tool_invocations.serving_host IS\n  'WHICH SERVICE served this call: the host label ''port-<n>'' (else ''pid-<n>'' when no port is resolvable), stable across restarts of the same logical service. Same vocabulary as stale-routine-executor''s condition keys, so pages and calls join. NULL = row predates migration 1043. See lib/serving-host-identity.ts.';\n\nCOMMENT ON COLUMN harness_shared.tool_invocations.serving_process_id IS\n  'WHICH RUN of that service: kernel-backed per-process identity ''linux:<boot-id>:<start-ticks>'', immune to the ~daily PID reuse on this box. Process boot time needs no column — it is min(invoked_at) GROUP BY this. NULL = unreadable, or row predates migration 1043.';\n\nCOMMENT ON COLUMN harness_shared.tool_invocations.serving_build_sha IS\n  'WHAT CODE that process had LOADED: short git sha, resolved once at boot. NULL means the row predates migration 1043 OR the process could not PROVE its loaded bytes (bundled artifact with no baked sha) — it is never the current checkout''s HEAD standing in for an unknown. Compare against tree HEAD to compute absolute code age; this is what makes host staleness measurable from the LEDGER, without cooperation from the stale process.';\n\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS tool_invocations_serving_host_idx\n  ON harness_shared.tool_invocations (serving_host, invoked_at DESC)\n  WHERE serving_host IS NOT NULL;\n","exit_code":0,"duration":{"secs":0,"nanos":41660}},"started_at_ms":1791596623973,"completed_at_ms":1791596623990}}
